title: Ten great things to do at Disney World for the holidays
summary:
By Jeffrey Siegal: Going to Walt Disney World has become a holiday tradition for our family, and we look forward to it every year. With the stunning decorations, festive events, and endless options for celebrating, it's one of my favorite times to visit.

Now, we don�t aim to do all 10 of these things every year, but we certainly try to check off a few - which always gives us something to look forward to the next time around. This list is not exhaustive or in any particular order, but I hope this list helps you get into the holiday spirit and to start planning your own traditions.

10. Christmas Tree Stroll � Starting November 11th and running until January 3rd, Disney Springs hosts its annual Christmas Tree Stroll, which features more than a dozen trees themed from Bluey all the way to Star Wars, scattered throughout the area. Pick up a free map at one of these locations and find your favorite one. I�m especially excited to see the special Hallmark tree.


Glimmering Greenhouses at EPCOT. Photos courtesy Disney, via the author

9. Living With the Land - Glimmering Greenhouses � I think this is one of the more underrated attractions in EPCOT. Adding holiday lighting and cheer to their large indoor greenhouse makes it look incredible, and it is best viewed at night.

8. Sleigh Ride at Fort Wilderness Resort and Campground � Take a ride through Fort Wilderness�s festive campground with a horse leading you on their �sleigh.� It�s Florida, so it doesn�t snow and the carriage actually has wheels, but for $80 it�s a fun, half-hour alternative to get into the winter spirit. It holds up to 4 adults or 2 adults and 3 small children.

7. Monorail Tour � This is one of the best ways to visit the three major hotels along the monorail loop: the Contemporary, Polynesian Village, and Grand Floridian. Each features unique, towering Christmas trees and decorations. Finish your tour at the Grand Floridian to take in the Victorian Christmas Experience and perhaps catch a castmember roasting chestnuts outside the main entrance.

6. Gingerbread House Tour � Taking place around mid-November, Disney�s BoardWalk Inn and Beach Club hotels feature talented artists showcasing their homebuilding skills in the form of massive gingerbread displays. As a bonus, check out the Yacht Club Resort for their own miniature display.


Disney's Hollywood Tower Hotel at Christmas

5. Walking Down Sunset Blvd � We all know how much of our yuletide decorating spirit is drawn from movies, and Disney built Sunset Blvd to capture the Golden Era of Hollywood which has provided so much in terms of Christmas style. Stroll down the famous street decked out in tinsel and vintage storefronts, and gaze upon the once-a-year colored Hollywood Tower Hotel. It�s great to take it all in while standing there waiting for it to �snow.�

4. Cookie Stroll � If you�ve ever wondered why Ree Drummond and Eddie Jackson get to have all the fun eating every Christmas cookie imaginable, then look no further than EPCOT from November 27th to December 30th. Each year during the EPCOT Festival of the Holidays, several pavilions sell special cookies and pastries to celebrate the sweetest time of the year. Past favorites have featured Linzer tarts, rugelach, and more.


EPCOT's Candlelight Processional

3. Candlelight Processional � Originating at Disneyland in 1958 and expanding to EPCOT in 1994, this moving tradition features various celebrities reading the Christmas story, accompanied by an awe-inspiring choir of over 300 singers and a full orchestra. It lasts around 45 minutes. You don't need a separate ticket to see it, but booking a dining package is highly recommended if you want a guaranteed seat.

2. Holiday Golf Cart Extravaganza � Each Christmas Eve at Fort Wilderness Resort and Campground, campers decorate their golf carts and parade them around the area. This is a self-run, unofficial Disney parade that is a blast to participate in or watch. However, because access to resort hotels has been restricted in recent years, you will need a dining reservation or a resort stay to check it out. Otherwise, you can catch videos of the spectacle online.


Jingle Cruise at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom

1. Jingle Cruise � The holiday overlay for the queue and ride is one of my absolute favorites. The cast members go all out down to the boat names, and the festive decorations make the entire experience amazing. You don't need a ticket to a Mickey�s Very Merry Christmas Party to check it out. Just ride it on a non-party night and you'll still be able to witness all the holiday fun.

Disney fans, what else would you include?

title: Rope Drop: It's beginning to feel like Christmas
summary:
By Robert Niles: As the "rope drop" starts a day at theme parks, the Sunday "Rope Drop" post kicks off the week here at Theme Park Insider. Here is what lies ahead for fans at the parks this week.

With Halloween now over, it's time for the Christmas holiday season at theme parks around the world. Sorry, Thanksgiving. The turkey firewall once again has failed to hold back Santa and his elfish minions from theme park domination.

The season starts Friday with the opening of Smoky Mountain Christmas at Dollywood and the Christmas Celebration at SeaWorld Orlando. SeaWorld is bringing back its Miracles orca show for the first time since the pandemic, joining the Sesame Street Christmas Parade, Elmo's Christmas Wish Show, Winter Wonderland on Ice, the Sea of Trees and the nightly Holiday Reflections: Fireworks Finale.

On Saturday, Walt Disney World kicks off its first hard-ticket party of the season with Disney Jollywood Nights at Disney's Hollywood Studios while An Old Time Christmas returns at Silver Dollar City. The Missouri park debuts its new Stars, Lights & Christmas Nights Parade this year.

Then one week from tonight, on November 8, Mickey's Very Merry Christmas Party returns at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom. You can find our complete list of theme park holiday events on our theme park events calendar.

Refurbishments

Redwood Creek Challenge Trail has closed at Disney California Adventure, as the Disneyland Resort prepares for its Holidays celebration starting November 13. It's a Small World also is closed at Disneyland through the 12th.

In Orlando, Tiana�s Bayou Adventure closes tomorrow at Walt Disney World�s Magic Kingdom for a refurbishment scheduled through December 17.

Tomorrow is the last call for the Animal Actors on Location show, which is closing permanently at Universal Studios Florida. Then on Wednesday, Hogwarts Express will be closed for the day at Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure.

Keep in touch and support the site

To keep up to date with more travel and theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's weekly newsletter.

And to help support Theme Park Insider while saving money, please shop our international and U.S. attraction ticket partners. Or contact our travel agent for a free, no-obligation vacation quote.

Remember that whenever you buy tickets or book vacations through our partners, a small portion of that goes to support Theme Park Insider. So you can support independent news while getting a great deal at the same time.

title: Walk Time: Looking ahead to IAAPA reveals
summary:
By Robert Niles: "Walk Time" is Theme Park Insider's Saturday look back at theme park news from the past week.

The annual TEA theme park attendance report dropped this week, with bad news for pretty much everyone outside Dollywood and Disneyland Paris. All of Six Flags' listed parks saw a drop in attendance last year, but the biggest percentage decline happened at Universal Studios Hollywood, which was down 8% due to the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, the collapse of international visitation to the US, and a decline in local entertainment industry employment. Attendance slides at top theme parks worldwide in 2025.

Jake and I talked about the attendance report in this week's episode of the Theme Park Insider Podcast: Why theme park attendance is down, and how to fix it.

Other TPI readers joined the conversation on the Discussion Forum: How to fix the Orlando Attendance Issue?

In other news, Six Flags shocked much of the coaster fan community by announcing that Six Flags Magic Mountain lands ArieForce One. The RMC coaster will open at the Southern California theme park in 2028, as part of what the park president is calling "one of the largest transformations ever undertaken in the park�s history."

On the flip side, we also are getting Layoffs at Disney, with 159 cast members being laid off at WDI HQ in Glendale, including Imagineering and Disney Live Entertainment. US theme park, Paris, and cruise line projects do not appear to be affected, but I am concerned for a delay in the Shanghai second gate project now.

We also got a couple of opening dates this week for projects at Disney parks in Asia: Tokyo Disney sets opening date for Wreck-It-Ralph ride and Shanghai Disneyland sets opening date for new hotel.

New theme park tech

It's always fun to see what might be coming next to the parks by looking at new patent applications from Disney and Universal.

First, Disney detailed its next generation of flying theater rides, which uses seats mounted to a floor rather than suspended from overhead: Get ready for a new way to 'fly' in Disney theater shows.

Don't have someone to hold your stuff and follow you around while you ride multiple roller coasters? Universal has a new solution that's out of this (Jurassic) world: Let a dinosaur hold your stuff while you ride a roller coaster.

What's up at IAAPA

IAAPA has revealed its schedule for press conferences at the annual IAAPA Expo, which opens November 16 in Orlando. Looks like we can expect coaster train reveals from:

  • Lagoon Amusement Park's Hot Racer, from Intamin
  • Six Flags Magic Mountain's Thrill Glider, from Vekoma
  • Holiday World's Cannonball!, from Mack Rides
  • Silver Dollar City's Miner's Mountain Express, also from Mack Rides

In addition, Gravity Group will unveil what it is calling the "world�s largest indoor wooden coaster," at over three stories tall with 1,130 feet of track and 11 airtime moments. This one is expected to go to Kentucky Kingdom.

In other announcements,

  • Busch Gardens Williamsburg and Brogent Technologies will talk about the Return to Corkscrew Hill simulator experience coming to the park next year.
  • Sally Dark Rides will show off the debut installation of its new Mini dark ride concept, which is coming to Doha Quest in Qatar as Guardians of the Hidden Chamber.
  • Maurer Rides is planning to announce a new roller coaster featuring its Spike Coaster technology, coming to "a leading U.S. attraction operator."

Finally, it appears that Falcon's Beyond has taken over development of the long-delayed Mattel Adventure Park at VAI Resort in Glendale, Ariz. The Orlando-based entertainment and technology firm has scheduled a press conference in which it "will unveil the next chapter of Mattel Adventure Park, revealing an expanded vision for the Arizona destination. The announcement will showcase how the expanded park and themed hospitality experiences will transform the project into an even more ambitious, multi-day entertainment destination."

And, oh yeah, Happy Halloween everyone!

title: Let a dinosaur hold your stuff while you ride a roller coaster
summary:
By Robert Niles: Need someone to hold your stuff when you visit a theme park? Universal has a new plan to help you.

For years, theme and amusement parks have offered lockers next to their thrill rides. When parks are playing nice, use of the lockers is free, but some parks charge people to stow their phones, packs and other loose items that are prohibited on certain roller coasters and rides.

Advanced locker systems offer two sides, so you can leave your items in the queue and then pick them up when exiting, without having to double back. But you still need to use a different locker for each attraction that requires them.

If you have a non-rider in your group, you could load them up with all the riders' loose items. Or you could rent some centrally located locker in the park. But what if you don't have a non-rider in your group and you don't want to have to walk all the way across the park to retrieve your stuff?

Enter Universal's proposed "Autonomous Vehicle Locker Utilization Systems and Methods," as described in the company's new patent application this week.

If you have stayed at Universal's Aventura Hotel, you might have encountered the robots than roam the hotel's lobby and make deliveries to guest rooms. Now, think of that, but put the robot in one of the Universal theme parks and task it with holding your stuff while you ride.

Because the robot can move, you can store you stuff at one location, then have the robot move and meet you at another location after you've ridden. With a guest identification system added to the mix, the robot would be able to find you and ID you to release your items when you meet up.

For fun, Universal also proposes theming the autonomous locker vehicles to various characters. Imagine a dinosaur rolling up to give you back your phone and pack after riding Jurassic World VelociCoaster and the Jurassic Jurassic Park River Adventure.


Image from Universal's patent application

You can read the full details of Universal's proposal and how it would work in its patent application: Autonomous Vehicle Locker Utilization Systems and Methods.

For more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's weekly newsletter.

title: Shanghai Disneyland sets opening date for new hotel
summary:
By Robert Niles: Shanghai Disney Resort has set the opening date for its new hotel - the resort's third.

Shanghai Disney Enchanted Star Hotel will open to guests on December 16. Reservations will open at midnight local time on November 6. The 400-room premium hotel is decorated in Art Nouveau style and stands on the shore of the resort's Wishing Star Lake, next to the Shanghai Disneyland Hotel.

The hotel will feature the first outdoor swimming pool at the Shanghai Disney Resort among its amentities, which include indoor swimming facilities, fitness centers and indoor and outdoor themed play areas, as well as shopping and dining locations. Guests staying at the Shanghai Disneyland Hotel will be able to use the facilities at the new Shanghai Disney Enchanted Star Hotel, and vice versa.

The third hotel in Shanghai Disney's portfolio is the mid-priced Toy Story Hotel, where I stayed when I visited the park for its 10th anniversary last summer.

Shanghai Disney has been developing a second gate at the resort, which has not yet been announced officially. Shanghai Disneyland this week captured the number five spot in the global theme park industry's annual attendance report, demonstrating the consumer demand that has inspired the expansion of the resort, which is jointly owned by Disney and China's Shendi Group.

For more theme park news, please sign up for Theme Park Insider's weekly newsletter.

title: Six Flags Magic Mountain lands ArieForce One
summary:
By Robert Niles: Six Flags is sending its recently acquired ArieForce One roller coaster to Magic Mountain.

My colleague Brady MacDonald at the Orange County Register just broke the news. Six Flags Magic Mountain will be the new home for the acclaimed Rocky Mountain Construction roller coaster that opened in 2023 at Fun Spot America Atlanta, in Georgia.

The first track elements for the coaster arrived at Magic Mountain today, with the trains undergoing refurbishment at RMC's facility in Idaho. ArieForce One will open at Six Flags Magic Mountain in 2028, though we do not know yet where in the park the ride will be installed.

That makes two coasters in two years for Magic Mountain, following next year's opening of Thrill Glider, the world's first installation of that new Vekoma model. The last new coaster to open at Magic Mountain was 2022's Wonder Woman Flight of Courage, which, like ArieForce One, was created by RMC.

ArieForce One will be the park's third RMC, joining Twisted Colossus, the rebuild of Colossus that opened in 2015.

"Relocating and reconstructing a coaster of this scale is a significant undertaking and there is substantial planning and engineering work still ahead," Magic Mountain President Brian Oerding told the Register.

Six Flags announced last month that it had bought the coaster following the closure of the Fun Spot America Atlanta park. ArieForce One is a 3,400-foot IBox coaster with four inversions, a 146-foot drop and a top speed of 64 mph. It placed number 37 worldwide among roller coasters in our latest annual Theme Park Insider reader survey. That would make it Magic Mountain's second-highest-rated coaster after Twisted Colossus, now that X2 has closed.

title: Get ready for a new way to 'fly' in Disney theater shows
summary:
By Robert Niles: Disney has plans for a new style of flying theater ride. Unlike its current Soarin' flying theater, where seats are suspended from an overhead support, Disney' proposed new design would mount seats to a floor, which would rotate forward to leave rows of viewers hanging above one another.

The plans are detailed in a new patent application published today, simply titled Flying Theater Ride. In this design, riders would step onto the theater platform like they were entering a traditional theater. Once seated, the floor of the theater would begin rotating into a vertical position.


Images from Disney's patent application

The seats would be mounted on axes that would allow them to maintain a level, forward-facing position as the floor underneath them rotated to vertical. As a result, once the floor's rotation was complete, instead of sitting behind the row in front of you, you now would be sitting above them.


In show position

This configuration eliminates the problem on Soarin', where riders in the back two rows can see the feet of the people in the rows ahead of them. With a stacked vertical theater, everyone would enjoy a clear, unobstructed view of the screen. Disney's patent application details the engineering behind the system, which requires counterweights and a variety of mechanisms to ensure that the rotation is smooth and stable. You can read the patent application here: Flying Theater Ride.

Who wants a villain's brew?

In another patent application published today, Disney described its new plans for creating a smoking beverage.

Typically, people use dry ice when they need to create fog or mist effect. But dry ice can be hazardous if handled improperly and it doesn't last long. If you want to sell a villain's brew that keeps smoking for the whole meal, you need a different solution.

Disney proposed its plans for such a set-up in Vapor Generating Device for Thematic Environments. The plan calls for a wicking device and vibration generator to draw fluid to generate vapor. A lighting element could add to the effect. The vapor generation could sit atop or be embedded in a beverage container or some other food item that would be served by a smoke- or fog-emitting effect.

Sounds like a food and beverage upsell opportunity in Villains Land, right?
